question.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $x≡43\,(\text{mod}\,14)?$
question.worked_solution:
When we add zero to both sides of a congruence modulo $n$, we can form an equivalent congruence by writing zero as an integer multiple of $n.$ This works because every integer multiple of $n$ is congruent to zero modulo $n.$

In our case, we add zero to both sides of the congruence and then use the fact that  $14\cdot (-3)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,14)$ to rewrite the right-hand side, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+0 & ≡43+0\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\ x & ≡43+0\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\  & ≡43+14\cdot (-3)\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\  & ≡43-42\, & (\text{mod}\,14) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,14)\end{aligned}
$$
